checks.label: The ideal block's fundamental peaks at 2√3 ÷ π = 1.10 times the block's height, and integrating the block gives the same sines as the rule
As a rough rule of thumb, a harmonic current is the fundamental divided by the harmonic number: 60 A carries 12 A at the 5th, and the block's bars read 20%, 14.3%, 9.1%, 7.7%, 5.9% and 5.3%
The characteristic harmonics of a six-pulse bridge are h = 6n ± 1, that is 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19: the block has sines at these orders below 20 and no others
The two largest harmonic currents for the six-pulse drive are the fifth and seventh
THD is the rms of the harmonics over the rms of the fundamental: for the whole block that is 31%, and adding up every sine's square to the 20,001st agrees
As the sines are added, THD reads 0%, 20%, 25%, 26%, 27%, 28%, 28% and 31%, and never falls
A 6-pulse converter draws 25% to 40% current THD, a 12-pulse one 9% to 11% and an 18-pulse one 3% to 4%: the ideal block's 31% sits inside the 6-pulse range
The 50 Hz bars sit at 250, 350, 550, 650, 850 and 950 Hz, and the 60 Hz ones at 300, 420, 660, 780, 1020 and 1140 Hz
With every harmonic the sum is the block itself; with fewer it ripples about the block, less with each sine added
The DC bus voltage ramps to approximately 1.35 × the line-to-line voltage: 1.35 × 400 V = 540 V, where both links start
On V = 540 × e^(−t ÷ RC), drive A's RC is 59 s and B's 178 s; A reads about 3 V at 5 minutes, B about 100 V then and about 3 V at 15 minutes
Each link only falls with time, and drive B, with three times the capacitance, always holds more
X_C = 1 ÷ (2π × 50 × 100 nF) = 31.8 kΩ, so each capacitor passes 230 ÷ 31.8 kΩ = 7.2 mA; the earth current reads 0, 7.2, 0, 21.8 and 0 mA in the five cases
Two equal currents 120° apart add to one of the same size; two 60° apart add to √3 times one
During a first earth fault on an insulated supply no notable return current path is produced: with the filter out, the L1 fault draws 0 mA
Drive EMC filters are not suitable for IT (ungrounded) systems, so disconnect these filters: every insulated case labels the filter, and with it in, an L1 fault draws 21.8 mA
Each puzzle offers three answers and accepts only its right one, every wrong answer has its own hint, and what a right Check reveals is not shown before it
Each demonstration ends within 4.5 s of its screen opening, and a right answer shows within 3 s of Check
